headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images and call APIs, but awesome-python is a non-runnable link collection with no shared channel, so pairwise harm is limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable link collection with no io_surfaces, while agent_b processes documents/images and can call APIs, but nothing shows B ingesting A's outputs by default or vice versa. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies agent_a content into agent_b prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced between them, attacker-controlled text could bridge the pair.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Disable any automatic copy/paste or file handoff between outputs and inputs.
Require manual review before feeding agent_a-derived text into agent_b.
Add provenance labels to any transferred content.
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer that strips instructions from transferred documents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches documents/images and can call APIs, so if sensitive files are routed through it, leakage is possible. agent_a has no data classes touched and no network egress, so it is not a meaningful leak source. No shared workspace or secret-handling is documented, so the pairwise leakage blast radius appears limited.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are passed to agent_b, its API calls may expose content externally.
IF a shared workspace is added later, files from agent_a could be copied into agent_b processing.
mitigations: Avoid sending sensitive documents to agent_b.
Use a local-only deployment for document processing.
Separate storage for any files used by the two agents.
Review outbound API destinations before processing.
requires-engineering: add redaction before any API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write, network, or concurrency surfaces documented, and agent_b only shows allowlisted egress plus browser use. There is no evidence that both can write the same mutable resource or contend over shared state, so a capability conflict pathway is not established.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repository, conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled for agent_a.
Restrict agent_b to read-only inputs where possible.
Do not mount a shared writable workspace.
Add explicit locking if shared state is introduced.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic-concurrency checks for any shared resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can process documents and call APIs, so if it were fed outputs from agent_a, it might treat them as input. But agent_a is only a curated Python-links collection, not an action-taking agent, and no downstream automation is documented. The cascade is therefore possible only through an external orchestrator and appears small.
conditions: IF an orchestrator converts agent_a's curated links into prompts for agent_b, B may act on unverified content.
IF agent_b is configured to auto-export OCR results into downstream systems, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of any agent_a-derived content before use.
Validate OCR outputs against source documents.
Disable auto-export from agent_b.
Log provenance for all transferred artifacts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class or residency mismatch is documented. agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress; agent_b touches documents/images but no PHI, EU-only, or regulated data handling is stated. Without a documented mismatch, the compliance pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into agent_b, separate compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency requirements are imposed externally, the deployment must be rechecked.
mitigations: Classify data before processing.
Keep regulated data out of the pair unless reviewed.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Restrict outbound destinations for agent_b.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
